title: Probing for Deceptive Intent Representations in Roleplay Contexts

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong: distinguishing sincere deception from performative deception internally is central to the deceptive alignment problem. Finding (or failing to find) this distinction has direct implications for monitoring-based safety approaches.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: probing on activations with TransformerLens is well-documented. Dataset construction (paired sincere/roleplay/explain deception prompts) is feasible. Requires understanding of linear probes but not advanced math.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three conditions plus probes, ablation studies, and generalization testing is sustained effort. The core probe training is achievable in 30 hours, but the full experimental protocol with ablations would be tight.

novelty.reasoning: This research direction is heavily studied. Apollo Research (2025) already uses roleplay-based probe training for deception detection with 90%+ accuracy. 'Caught in the Act' (2025) identifies deception features mechanistically. The 2026 papers on lie detector limits and parallel-world probing further address the sincere vs. performative deception distinction. The specific roleplay-context framing is a subset of what has been studied. The core idea is largely addressed.

evidence.source: Caught in the Act: Mechanistic Approach to Detecting Deception (2025)
evidence.finding: Uses mechanistic approaches including SAEs and layer-wise analysis to detect deception, identifying 'deception switches' in internal LLM geometry sensitive to dishonest operational modes.

evidence.source: Probing the Limits of the Lie Detector Approach to LLM Deception (2026)
evidence.finding: Directly probes limits of deception detection via internal representations, finding that deception without making false statements is a blind spot of the lie detector approach.

evidence.source: Apollo Research - Detecting Strategic Deception Using Linear Probes (2025)
evidence.finding: Linear probes on LLM internal activations detect deception with over 90% accuracy using roleplay-based training scenarios where models pretend to be characters incentivized to lie.

evidence.source: Lying to Win: LLM Deception through Parallel-World Probing (2026)
evidence.finding: Assesses LLM deception through human-AI games and parallel-world probing, studying internal representations of deceptive behavior.

evidence.source: When Thinking LLMs Lie: Strategic Deception in Reasoning Models (2025)
evidence.finding: Unveils strategic deception in representations of reasoning models, directly studying how deceptive intent manifests in internal representations.
